inline_comments.comment: The new `log.debug` message duplicates information already present on the two immediately preceding lines (`log.debug('Invalid date:' + str)` and `log.debug('With date format:' + dateFormat.trim())`). Repeating the same facts in a slightly different template adds noise without providing additional diagnostic value. Remove this extra call, or consolidate all three into a single message.

`getEstimatedTickCount` is declared as a `function` statement inside `draw()`, but it closes over no variables from `draw`'s scope — its only inputs are its explicit parameters. Placing it inside `draw()` means it is logically re-created on every render call and is invisible to module-level tests. Move it to module scope alongside the other helpers (e.g., near `getMaxIntersections`). This makes it independently testable and signals clearly that it is a pure utility.

When the top-axis tick count exceeds `MAX_TICK_COUNT`, the block silently falls through without any log output, unlike the corresponding bottom-axis path which emits a `log.warn`. This asymmetry makes it harder to diagnose rendering issues — a developer inspecting logs would see the bottom-axis warning but have no indication the top axis was also affected. Add the same `log.warn` call here, or extract the warning into the shared `getEstimatedTickCount` call site to guarantee consistent behavior for both axes.

Per project changeset conventions, the first word of the description after the type prefix must be capitalized (e.g., `fix: Validate dates and tick interval...` instead of `fix: validate dates...`). Incorrect casing can cause changeset tooling to process the entry incorrectly.

general_comments.comment: The `getEstimatedTickCount` function uses `dayjs.duration({ [interval]: every })` where `interval` comes directly from the regex capture group. The regex already enforces that `interval` is one of `millisecond | second | minute | hour | day | week | month`, so the `?? 'day'` nullish-coalescing fallback in `interval ?? 'day'` is unreachable. While harmless, it could mislead a reader into thinking `interval` can be `null` or `undefined` at the call site. Remove the fallback and document that the function expects only values already validated by the regex.

The tick-count guard logic (`getEstimatedTickCount` call + `MAX_TICK_COUNT` comparison + `switch`) is duplicated verbatim for the bottom axis and the top axis. Consider extracting a helper such as `applyTickInterval(axis, every, interval, minTime, maxTime)` that contains this shared logic. This would eliminate the repeated `domain` lookup (see inline comment), ensure the bottom and top axes are always kept in sync (including the missing warning on the top path), and reduce the overall diff surface for future changes.
